From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@greenfieldhealth.com>

Subject: Inference dependencies, KV-cache provenance and SIG request

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — Greenfield is running a vendor SIG-lite and we need a scoped response covering subprocessor provenance for the inference stack that Redwood will be touching. The specific asks from our security team: 1) a consolidated subprocessor roster (CSV) listing providers used for "inference runtime" (KV/prefix caches, telemetry/observability, metrics ingestion, and any third-party model hosting we rely on), 2) residency and encryption posture for cached artifacts (in transit and at rest), and 3) current SOC 2 Type II attestation and any CAIQ/CAIQ-lite mapping you can share.

We attached the SIG-lite questionnaire (SIG-questionnaire_Greenfield.xlsx) — if you can return a CSV + the signed attestation by end of next week that would keep our procurement timeline intact. Also we have a couple of clarifying Qs in the sheet around ephemeral key management and any shared-key services used for KV caches.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Senior Information Security Manager
Greenfield Health

Attachment: SIG-questionnaire_Greenfield.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks Jonas — a few clarifying questions from our security reviewer before you finalize the sheet:

1) KV cache hosting: is the prefix/KV cache a Redwood-managed service running in our customer-specific tenancy, or is it served by a third-party caching provider (e.g., managed Redis by a cloud vendor or a specialized cache operator)? If third-party, we need the provider name, country of operation, and whether the cache is encrypted at rest by the provider or by Redwood.

2) Ephemeral keys: does Redwood rotate ephemeral keys on a per-session basis and store them in customer-controlled KMS, or does Redwood manage a multi-tenant KMS for ephemeral secret signing/rotation?

3) Telemetry and logs: are any raw request/response traces forwarded to a third-party observability vendor (Datadog, Sentry, Honeycomb, etc.)? If yes, which vendor and what minimal retention do you apply to traces that include prompt/response or hash pointers?

4) Evidence: for the KV cache encryption claim we would prefer an architecture diagram or short note that shows the encryption-in-transit and at-rest controls for the cache. A one-page architecture PNG is great. Also if you have a direct DocuSign link for a data-handling addendum / attest, please include.

If it's easier we can accept the SIG-lite workbook first and then a targeted follow-up for the remaining evidence. Our requested final date is 2026-12-08 EOD.

Thanks,
Priya Sethi
Security Analyst
Greenfield Health

Subject: Re: Inference dependencies, KV-cache provenance and SIG request

Priya / Elena — thanks for the follow-ups. Answers inline below and attached deliverables.

-- Answers (concise) --
1) KV cache hosting:
Jonas: Our KV/prefix cache is a Redwood-managed service running inside the customer VPC when customers opt for Private mode (VPC/on-prem). For Hosted customers we default to a dedicated, single-tenant cache cluster in the same cloud region as the inference workers; the cache itself is provisioned on managed cloud instances (we use managed Redis clusters from the cloud provider for ephemeral caching in Hosted mode). For any managed Redis instance we layer application-level encryption before writing sensitive keys; at-rest encryption is enabled by the managed provider. Country of operation is the cloud region selected by the customer (we annotate this in the CSV).

2) Ephemeral keys:
Jonas: Ephemeral session tokens are generated by Redwood and rotated per-session. Cryptographic material for those tokens is sealed using our customer-dedicated KMS keys when customers use Private mode; for Hosted customers, we use customer-specific envelopes with KMIP-backed keys managed in our HSM-backed KMS. We will include a short KMS flow diagram as requested.

3) Telemetry and logs:
Jonas: We send aggregated metrics to Datadog (metric names only) for hosted infra and use Honeycomb for internal trace sampling. Raw prompt/response payloads are not forwarded to third parties. Any traces sent to a third-party are redacted at the application layer and retention is 30 days by default; we can adjust retention via contract for enterprise customers.

4) Evidence & artifacts provided:
- redwood_inference_subprocessors_2026-12.csv (full roster with provider country and encryption columns)
- SOC2_Type2_Attestation_2025.pdf (attestation cover page)
- SIG-lite_responses_2026.xlsx (completed workbook mapped to your sheet)
- infra_kv_cache_architecture.png (one-page diagram showing in-transit and at-rest controls)

We also uploaded a CAIQ-lite mapping in the Drive folder. DocuSign link for our standard Data Processing Addendum is: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef123456. If you want an encrypted exchange of the architecture PNG, tell us and we will provision a secured share.

Ben and Marissa — flagged for any additional redactions or follow-up Qs.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Vendor Risk & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_inference_subprocessors_2026-12.csv, SOC2_Type2_Attestation_2025.pdf, SIG-lite_responses_2026.xlsx, infra_kv_cache_architecture.png
